thread:
sre-oncall: FYI APS2a pool dropped ~25% available GPUs in last 10m, automated hotspare swap kicked but we're seeing failures on swap.
alyssa: seeing repeated `GPU ECC UNCORRECTABLE` on node gpu-node-341, logs show NVLINK errors + device reset loop.
dan: can we cordon/drain that node? impact to in-flight requests?
sre-oncall: cordon now, will drain. prefer graceful: `kubectl drain gpu-node-341 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force` then re-route.
infra-bot: Initiating drain: gpu-node-341 by sre-oncall at 1918203470. Eviction in progress.
marco: hotspare rotation failing because hotspare instances in same AZ are hitting allocation quota. we need to either shift to APS1 fallback or trigger cross-AZ autoscaler.
alyssa: if we shift to APS1 that's +~20% cost and adds ~40ms median tail. is that acceptable for canary traffic?
dan: prefer keep latency SLOs. route only non-latency-critical traffic to APS1. use routing policy `weight: non-critical=0.3`.
ops-runner: created a temporary placement in APS2b (different AZ) with 4 x gpus (preemptible) to relieve pressure. preemptible risk noted.
alyssa: preemptible acceptable short-term if we use multi-variant fallback. switch model variant to quantized-8 to reduce footprint while we rebuild node.
marco: make sure caching keys are warmed after model swap. if we send cold requests to quantized model we might spike CPU. plan: 1) finish drain 2) attach hotspare APS2b 3) reroute 15% of background traffic 4) rebuild node 341 and replace board.
dan: can infra-bot update routing weights?
infra-bot: Updating routing: aps2a weight -0.15 -> aps2b +0.15 for non-critical routes. Confirmed at 1918203540.
sre-oncall: drain finished. Pod eviction summary: 12 running pods evicted, 2 failed to terminate and were force-deleted.
alyssa: rolling replace scheduled with hardware team: replacement part on order (GPU assembly). ETA 6h for on-site swap.
marco: while node is down we should tag it as REDZONE to avoid autoscaler reusing same rack. added meta: rack=R12 redzone=true.
ops-runner: started canary traffic shift: sending 10% of text-generation to APS1 region (non-critical). monitoring: token latency currently +32ms on that route.
dan: alerting: create a cost watch for APS1 spend, set threshold $50/hr until normal.
infra-bot: Cost watch created by dan: aps1-temp-threshold at $50/hr.
sre-oncall: ECC errors correlate with sudden thermal events at 04:22 UTC. RAS logs show repeated correctable->uncorrectable escalation. opening hardware incident INC-2026.
alyssa: adding SW mitigation: set driver to soft-reset-on-error false, enable GPU ECC scrubbing window to 1h (temp). apply during low traffic window 03:00-04:00 local.
marco: heads up to platform: if further nodes degrade, we need to pull capacity from Dedicated pools or pause low-priority batch jobs. prepping a list of batch queues to pause.
dan: paused batch: nightly-batch-ml, embeddings-reindex. freed ~6 GPUs.
ops-runner: hotspare APS2b handling now ~18% extra load. tail latency still within 95th for critical routes.
alyssa: once replacement board arrives we'll reprovision node with fresh image, run stress + memtest, then rejoin. will mark node as `maintenance` until verification complete.
sre-oncall: any ETA on hardware swap?
alyssa: courier ETA confirmed 5.5h on site, swap + verification 45m, plus image bake 30m => total 6.75h.
marco: schedule a postmortem if more than 4 nodes fail or incident extends beyond 8h.
dan: FYI notify account teams for customers on reserved capacity in APS2a — potential SLA noise. I'll draft a quick blurb.
infra-bot: Notifying teams: reserved-capacity-alert sent to #customers-ops at 1918203720.
sre-oncall: summary: node gpu-node-341 cordoned/drained, hotspare rotation -> APS2b provisioned, partial traffic reroute to APS1 for non-critical, cost watch up. hardware replace in progress (ETA ~6.75h). monitoring+alerts active.
marco: leaving this thread open for updates. ping when node back in cluster or if hotspare preempted.
ops-runner: will post timeline updates every 15m or on state change. :hourglass_flowing_sand:
